`label`: show or set a device's label.

## Synopsis

<strong>label</strong> <em>device</em> \[<em>label</em>\]

## Description

With only a <em>device</em>, <strong>label</strong> prints its label (nothing when it has none). With a <em>label</em>, it sets it; an empty one, <strong>""</strong>, clears it.

A <em>device</em> is named as <strong>lsdev</strong>(1) names it (<strong>storage0</strong>, <strong>eeprom</strong>), with or without <strong>/dev/</strong> before it, or by its id.

The label is kept on the device's item, and shown in its details (hold Shift over it), so it goes wherever the device goes. <strong>lsdev</strong> shows every device's label. A label is at most 32 printable characters.

## Exit status

0 when the label was printed or set; 1 for a device that isn't there, a label that can't be one, or a device that can't have one (a cabled block's: it has no item to keep it on).

## Examples

```text
label storage1 backups
label eeprom
label storage1 ""
```

## Notes

Linux labels a disk's filesystem (<strong>e2label</strong>, <strong>fatlabel</strong>); mcos labels any device that is an item, as OpenOS did.

## See also

<strong>lsdev</strong>(1)
